TRIPWIRE_NODE_GROUP.description: Optional Tripwire Enterprise node-group filter — friendly group name (alphanumeric + spaces + ._- up to 128 chars, e.g. 'DC Tier-1 Windows Servers'). When set, the executor narrows /api/v1/computers via the nodeGroup query parameter AND re-checks nodeGroups[].name on each returned record client-side as a defence-in-depth fallback for TE consoles that silently ignore the parameter. Garbage / control-char input is logged + ignored (no filter applied) rather than fanned out into a 400. Leave blank to walk every managed node in the catalogue.

TRIPWIRE_RULE_TYPE.description: Optional Tripwire Enterprise rule-type filter. Accepts the canonical TE rule-type families plus common synonyms — compliance, configuration (synonym: config), policy (synonym: policy_check), file_integrity (synonyms: fim, integrity, fileintegrity), change (synonyms: changes, change_audit). Case-insensitive. Normalised client-side onto the canonical TE rule-type slug before being passed to /api/v1/elementVersions/findings via the ruleType query parameter. Garbage / control-char input is logged + ignored (no filter applied) rather than fanned out into a 400. Leave blank to pull every finding type.

TRIPWIRE_MIN_SEVERITY.description: Optional client-side severity floor for Tripwire Enterprise findings. Accepts info | low | medium | high | critical (plus TE synonyms: severe -> critical, major / important -> high, moderate / warning -> medium, minor -> low, informational / information / unspecified -> info) plus numeric-string CVSS-style input bucketed via severity_from_cvss (<4 low, <7 medium, <9 high, >=9 critical). Findings below the floor are dropped from the Faraday output after per-finding severity normalisation (bucketed from the freeform severity string enum + numeric severityScore / cvss 0-10 fallback). Defaults to info (no filtering).

name: tripwire_enterprise
title: Tripwire Enterprise (Compliance / FIM)
description: Tripwire Enterprise compliance / file-integrity-monitoring REST importer. Pulls the managed-node catalogue and the open compliance / FIM finding catalogue from a Tripwire Enterprise console via GET <TRIPWIRE_HOST>/api/v1/computers (paginated managed-node catalogue, optionally narrowed by nodeGroup=<TRIPWIRE_NODE_GROUP>) and GET <TRIPWIRE_HOST>/api/v1/elementVersions/findings (paginated finding catalogue, optionally narrowed by ruleType=<TRIPWIRE_RULE_TYPE>). Each TE-managed node becomes one Faraday host (keyed by the TE node identifier; carries the node's name / ipAddress / operatingSystem / make / model / nodeGroups / lastCheck / tags — TE's surface is node-scoped so the host record carries the underlying OS string, e.g. 'Microsoft Windows Server 2019 Standard'); each unresolved finding on that node attaches as a Faraday vulnerability with the engine prefix [CONFIG-MGMT]. Findings are joined back to the computer catalogue by nodeId / computerId; orphaned findings (assets present in TE-findings but absent from the narrowed computer catalogue) attach to a synthetic catch-all host so they're not silently dropped. Severity is bucketed from the freeform severity string enum (critical / high / medium / low / info plus TE synonyms severe / major / important / moderate / warning / minor / informational / unspecified) with the numeric severityScore / score / cvss / riskScore 0-10 used as a CVSS-style fallback. Status mapped from status / state / findingStatus / resolution (open / new / detected / unresolved / pending -> open, resolved / fixed / mitigated / promoted / approved / baselined / closed -> closed, acknowledged / accepted / deferred / waived / will_not_fix / false_positive / suppressed / dismissed / ignored -> risk-accepted; note: TE's 'promoted' lifecycle action means the change is now the new baseline so it maps onto closed). Pagination uses TE's canonical start + count cursor pattern (PAGE_SIZE=100 per page capped at MAX_PAGES=200 = 20k rows per endpoint) with totalCount exhaustion detection. Refs include Tripwire-Finding / Tripwire-Rule / Tripwire-RuleType / Tripwire-Policy / Tripwire-Test / Tripwire-Element / Tripwire-ElementVersion / Tripwire-Node / Tripwire-NodeId pivots plus inline advisory URLs. CVE list harvested via a strict CVE-\d{4}-\d+ regex from cve / cveId / cves / cveIds / details.cve fields plus title / summary / description / evidence / ruleDescription / remediation token scans. Auth: HTTP Basic with the TRIPWIRE_USER / TRIPWIRE_PASSWORD credentials carried as Authorization: Basic <b64(user:password)> + Accept: application/json on every call (built explicitly via base64.b64encode so the executor stays testable without a live requests install and the encoded credentials never leak into log output). TRIPWIRE_HOST is the Tripwire Enterprise console endpoint URL (http(s)://host[:port], trailing slash stripped client-side, control chars rejected). Tags: [tripwire, tripwire-enterprise, config-mgmt, compliance].
